To have Maryville College (MC) students count your service toward a course, your organization must be a **formal partner in a “Placement Model”** (the Community‑Engaged Learning or curricular‑service model).  

**What qualifies you as a host**

| Requirement | Source |
|-------------|--------|
| **Incorporated, structured organization** – board of directors, clear governance, funding sources, professional staff, and volunteer insurance | [4] |
| **Serve a marginalized or materially poor population** | [4] |
| **Provide on‑site staff presence and direct supervision** – clearly define the roles of agency staff and student interns/volunteers | [4] |
| **Offer orientation and necessary training** | [4] |
| **Complete end‑of‑year evaluations** | [4] |
| **Actively help students meet the learning objectives of the course** – the agency must be part of the course’s required service hours (Placement Model) | [3] |

When these conditions are met, the Center for Community Engagement can formalize the partnership so that the service hours count toward the student’s academic credit.

**How this differs from a one‑off volunteer opportunity**

| One‑off volunteer | Placement‑model host |
|-------------------|----------------------|
| Posted on Handshake or other ad‑hoc platforms | Requires a formal partnership with the Center for Community Engagement |
| No course credit; purely informal service | Service hours are integrated into a course’s learning objectives |
| No requirement for staff supervision, orientation, or evaluation | Must provide staff presence, defined roles, orientation, and end‑of‑year evaluation |
| Not tied to a curriculum or academic assessment | Directly supports the student’s academic progress and assessment |

In short, posting a one‑off volunteer opportunity is an informal, non‑credit activity, whereas hosting students for class credit demands a structured, evaluated partnership that aligns with a specific course’s learning goals.

answer:
The waiver (whether GPA or Testing) must be submitted **before the end of the semester that precedes the semester in which you will take EDU 351 Senior Study I**. This is the deadline specified for both types of waivers in the Education program.  

Source: Maryville College Educator Preparation Program – Waiver Request page. <https://www.maryvillecollege.edu/academics/divisions/education/waiver-request/>
